judgment.reasoning_summary: The given differential equation f'(x) = f(f(x)) implies that the derivative of f at any point x is equal to the value of f at the point f(x). This suggests that f must be a constant function because the derivative of a non-constant function cannot be equal to the function itself at all points. The only constant function that satisfies this condition is the zero function, as any non-zero constant would not satisfy the equation for all x.
